local_review.finding_body: In Micronaut_buffer_nettyTest.java, both ApplicationContext.run(...) calls enable asynchronous eager bean processing. The native test lane completed its assertions but then emitted an uncaught NullPointerException from DefaultBeanContext.processParallelBeans after the contexts had closed. This violates the test contract requirement that background resources be cleanly bounded and closed.
local_review.finding_title: Application context closes while eager bean processing is still running
local_review.fix_note: Changed both test contexts to use ApplicationContext.builder(...).eagerBeansEnabled(false).start(). The tests still resolve and assert the same container-managed beans, while avoiding the asynchronous eager-bean thread that raced with context shutdown. Re-ran formatting, style, metadata validation, JVM tests, native-image build, and native tests successfully; the uncaught exception no longer occurs.
local_review.review_comment: Reviewed the requested commit range and local evidence. The diff is limited to one io.micronaut:micronaut-buffer-netty:5.1.13 coordinate, uses only reachability-metadata.json, has a separate test package, exercises public library APIs rather than the scaffold, has a 30-second test bound, and contains no native-image skip/failure-tolerance pattern, test-side reflection shortcut, hardcoded version assertion, or JVM override. The reported 0/0 dynamic-access result is a valid no-calls case, so neither the percentage gate nor entry-count mismatch probe applies. I repaired an asynchronous ApplicationContext shutdown defect found during native execution. The resulting tree passes spotlessCheck, checkstyle, checkMetadataFiles, JVM tests, native-image compilation, and all 10 native tests without the prior background-thread exception.
